decisive_items: Krebs von den Lungen-6 level: 1250 U/mL (normal <500 U/mL)
Diffuse ground-glass opacity, mosaic attenuation, and ill-defined centrilobular nodules
response.rationale: Drug-induced pneumonitis best explains recurrent diffuse GGO, mosaic attenuation, and centrilobular nodules after repeated chemotherapy in a patient with elevated KL-6 and BAL lymphocytosis/eosinophilia. There is no radiation history, and hypersensitivity pneumonitis is less supported given negative anti-T. asahii antibodies and no clear exposure.

rejected.why: No radiation therapy is described in the vignette, so radiation pneumonitis lacks a necessary mechanism.
BAL lymphocytosis is present, but lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia typically requires autoimmune/CT features and does not explain the drug-related timing and KL-6 elevation.
Imaging and BAL could resemble hypersensitivity pneumonitis, but serum anti-T. asahii antibodies are negative and no exposure history is provided.
Organizing pneumonia can have GGO and nodules, but the BAL lymphocytosis, elevated KL-6, and recurrence after chemotherapy are more specific for drug-induced pneumonitis.
